draft.title: Coming of age
card: Coming of age is the move from childhood to adulthood. It is a change in how a person is seen and what is expected of them, not only a change in the body.
Cultures do not agree on when it happens. Some link it to a set age, and others link it to a life event or to taking on adult duties.
Cultures also differ in how they mark it. Some hold a formal event, some give new rights or responsibilities, and some do little to mark it at all.
In Australia, the law gives different adult rights at different ages. A person can vote at 18, but other rights, such as getting a driver licence, come at other ages.
draft.remember: Coming of age is a social change from child to adult, and cultures set its timing and marking in different ways.

a.q: Which statement best describes coming of age?
opts: A change in status from child to adult, seen differently by cultures
A change in body shape that happens at the same age everywhere
A formal event held at the age of 18 in every culture
The point at which a person first leaves their family home
a.why: Coming of age is about being seen as an adult and taking on adult expectations, and cultures differ on when and how. The option about the body is tempting, but the card says it is not only a change in the body, and the timing is not the same everywhere.
a.clue: Think about status and expectations, not only the body.

b.q: Ana is 15. In her community, a young person is treated as an adult once they start full-time work, and there is no ceremony. Her cousin Leo lives in a city where adulthood is linked to turning 18. What does this show about coming of age?
opts: Cultures can set different timing and signs of adulthood
One of the two communities has the wrong idea of adulthood
Coming of age only counts when a ceremony is held
Adulthood is decided by age in every modern city
b.why: Ana's community links adulthood to work and Leo's links it to age, so the timing and signs differ between cultures. The idea that coming of age needs a ceremony is tempting, but the card says some cultures do little to mark it.
b.clue: Compare what each community uses to decide who is an adult.
